worked_examples.problem: In-Text Question & Exercise (Section 7.1, 7.2 & p. 15): (a) What is the importance of DNA copying in reproduction? (b) Why is variation beneficial to a species even if it is not advantageous for the individual?
worked_examples.given: Cellular reproduction, genetic replication fidelity, and natural selection.
worked_examples.formula: DNA replication produces structural blueprints; Genetic variation enables evolutionary resilience under environmental niche shifts.
worked_examples.substitution: Biochemical replication errors generating natural phenotypic variation.
worked_examples.calculation:
(a) Importance of DNA copying: DNA contains hereditary instructions for synthesizing body proteins and structures. Copying DNA ensures that daughter cells receive identical structural blueprints to maintain tissue functioning and species fidelity.
(b) Evolutionary Benefit of Variation: If an entire population of organisms were genetically identical and inhabited a specific ecological niche, a catastrophic environmental change (e.g. sharp temperature spike, novel viral pathogen, drying of pond) could kill all individuals, causing species extinction. If genetic variants exist within the population (e.g. heat-resistant bacteria in a hot spring), those variants will survive the catastrophe and propagate, preventing the species from dying out.
worked_examples.finalAnswer: (a) DNA copying preserves structural blueprints across generations; (b) Genetic variation allows populations to survive unpredictable environmental disasters, preventing extinction.
worked_examples.image_search_query: dna replication importance reproduction variation natural selection

worked_examples.problem: In-Text Question & Exercise (Section 7.4 & p. 15): (a) What are the functions of the placenta during human gestation? (b) List three different methods of contraception and explain their working mechanisms.
worked_examples.given: Maternal-fetal uterine physiology; Reproductive health and family planning.
worked_examples.formula: Placenta villi countercurrent exchange; Barrier, chemical, and surgical contraceptive mechanisms.
worked_examples.substitution: Nutrient/gas exchange across maternal blood spaces.
worked_examples.calculation:
(a) Functions of Placenta: A specialized disc-shaped vascular organ embedded in the uterine wall. Chorionic villi on the fetal side provide huge surface area in maternal blood pools. Functions: 1. Delivers glucose, amino acids, and oxygen from mother to embryo. 2. Transports metabolic wastes (urea, uric acid, CO2) from embryo to maternal blood for excretion. 3. Endocrine gland secreting progesterone and human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG) to maintain pregnancy.
(b) Contraceptive Methods:
1. Barrier Methods (Condoms, diaphragms): Physically prevent sperm from entering the female cervix/uterus, while shielding against Sexually Transmitted Infections (STIs).
2. Hormonal / Chemical Methods (Oral contraceptive pills): Ingested hormones alter estrogen-progesterone balance, preventing ovulation from ovaries.
3. Surgical Methods (Vasectomy in males, Tubectomy in females): Tying and cutting the vas deferens or fallopian tubes permanently blocks gamete transit.
worked_examples.finalAnswer: (a) Placenta delivers nutrients/oxygen to embryo, removes metabolic wastes, and secretes hormones; (b) Barrier blocks sperm transit, hormonal stops ovulation, surgical cuts/ties gamete conduits.
